The proposed solution is incorrect.

### Reason for Rejection:
The proposed solution asserts that no non-straight staircase cuts can produce a new rectangle when the dimensions are coprime (even explicitly claiming that a $4 \times 9$ rectangle cannot be rearranged into another rectangle). 

This claim is false. For example, a $9 \times 4$ rectangle (where $\gcd(9, 4) = 1$) can be cut along grid lines using a staircase path moving only down and right—specifically from $(3, 4)$ down to $(3, 2)$, right to $(6, 2)$, and down to $(6, 0)$—dividing the rectangle into two pieces that slide to form a $6 \times 6$ square.

In general, for any factorization where the dimensions allow an $m$-step staircase sliding dissection, new rectangles can be formed (not only by straight midpoint cuts). Consequently, the conclusion that only $1$ new rectangle can be produced is incorrect.

VERDICT: REJECT
